primitives.name: Possession Tradeoff Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this work, we specifically evaluate the trade-off between trying to retain possession versus intentionally putting the ball out of play near the opponentʼs goal for a throw-in.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'Time interval (actions)', 'P_{\\text{retain}}': 'Probability of retaining possession', 'P_{\\text{throw}}': 'Probability of successful throw-in', 'G_{\\text{score}}': 'Expected goals from throw-in recovery'}
primitives.assumptions: Players act rationally to maximize expected goals; spatial bins define strategic regions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( P_{\text{retain}} < P_{\text{throw}} \cdot G_{\text{score}} \), boot-it is preferred.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian scoring model where \( P_{\text{throw}} \) is a latent variable conditioned on opponent pressure.

primitives.name: Throw-In Advantage Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: Regularly you see teams employing it as a kick-off strategy.1 The underlying belief is that an opponent throw-in in the corner of the pitch is worth more than established possession in the center of the pitch.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G_{\\text{score}}': 'Expected goals from throw-in', 'P_{\\text{lose}}': 'Probability of losing possession from center'}
primitives.assumptions: Throw-in location favors immediate pressing; center possession risks high-pressure loss.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ratio exceeds unity when opponent pressure is high and throw-in is near goal.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's spatial transition kernel, encoding positional advantage of throw-in over central pass.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of goals from throw-in recovery

primitives.name: Backward Pass Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Up until the early 2000s, this was a common refrain at soccer matches across all levels and age groups.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\theta': 'Angle between pass start and end positions (radians)'}
primitives.assumptions: Pass direction determines intent; backward pass implies low progressivity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Passes with \( |\theta| > \frac{5}{6}\pi \) are classified as backward.

layer2.telemetry: Frequency of backward passes per game

reasoning_traces.think:
The boot-it strategy emerges from a probabilistic optimization framework where the decision to kick the ball out of bounds is modeled as a stochastic choice between two outcomes: retaining possession or initiating a throw-in. The core operator is the possession tradeoff function T(P_retain, P_throw, G_score), which evaluates the expected value of each action. When the probability of scoring from a throw-in exceeds the risk of losing possession from a central pass, the boot-it strategy becomes optimal. This is formalized through a ratio-based comparison: G_score/P_lose > 1. The backward pass classifier serves as a binary indicator of tactical intent, filtering for non-progressing plays. These primitives form a dual structure: one for strategic decision-making (tradeoff) and another for behavioral categorization (classification). Failure modes arise when spatial assumptions break down or when pressure dynamics misalign with historical data.
